body:
What actually matters in a TV under ₹15,000

Skip the marketing. Three specs decide if a budget TV actually works in 2026: OS smoothness (Google TV beats custom shells), panel type (VA has better contrast than TN), and Wi-Fi stability (single-band 2.4GHz is fine for OTT). Everything else — refresh rate, HDR — is fluff at this price.

We compared six smart TVs under ₹15,000 from Xiaomi, Realme, OnePlus, Acer, Hisense, and Kodak. Here's what we found — and one model you should avoid even though it claims WebOS at under ₹10K.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the Xiaomi TV 5A. It's the only budget TV in 2026 with Google TV that actually responds without lag, and 20W speakers that fill a small room without distortion.

Our picks: 5 smart TVs that actually deliver

⭐ Top Pick

1. Xiaomi TV 5A 32-inch HD Ready Google TV

₹12,999
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound20W
OSGoogle TV
Warranty2 yr

Xiaomi's 2026 entry-level model is the smoothest in this range. Google TV is responsive, the remote is minimal but functional, and you get 2 years of guaranteed software updates. The VA panel has better contrast than IPS rivals. Speakers are tuned louder than average at 20W.

Pros

  • Google TV is the cleanest interface in this price range
  • 2-year warranty — most rivals stop at 1 year
  • 20W speakers — louder than Realme and Acer equivalents
  • VA panel gives deeper blacks for movies

Cons

  • HD-ready (1366x768) — text can look soft up close
  • No Dolby Vision (only HDR10)
  • Single HDMI 2.0 port — soundbar takes the second one
Runner Up

2. Realme Smart TV 32-inch HD Google TV

₹11,499
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound24W
OSGoogle TV
Warranty1 yr

Realme punches above its weight on sound — 24W Dolby Audio is the loudest in this roundup. Google TV is responsive. The trade-off is build quality: the bezel is glossy plastic and the stand feels light. Software updates have been patchy after the first year.

Pros

  • 24W speakers — the loudest in this roundup
  • Google TV with Chromecast built-in
  • Three HDMI ports (one with ARC)

Cons

  • Only 1-year warranty
  • Glossy bezel scratches easily
  • Software updates inconsistent after 12 months

3. OnePlus Y1S 32-inch HD Ready

₹13,999
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound20W
OSAndroid 11
Warranty1 yr

OnePlus' cheapest TV is solid but not standout. Android 11 is clean, build quality is the best in the roundup (metal frame, sturdy stand), and OxygenPlay 2.0 has decent content discovery. The downside: ₹13,999 is ₹2,000 more than the Xiaomi for almost identical performance.

Pros

  • Premium build — metal frame, sturdy stand
  • OxygenPlay 2.0 surfaces content from multiple apps
  • Auto low-latency mode for casual gaming

Cons

  • ₹13,999 vs ₹12,999 Xiaomi — hard to justify
  • Only Android 11, not the newer Google TV
  • Single-band Wi-Fi — buffering on weak networks

4. Acer 32-inch H Series HD Smart TV

₹10,999
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound20W
OSAndroid 11
Warranty1 yr

The cheapest TV in this roundup, and it shows. Android 11 works but is sluggish compared to Google TV on the Xiaomi. Build is functional, sound is average, and Acer's service network is thinner than Xiaomi or Realme. Best for users who want absolute lowest price and don't mind occasional UI stutter.

Pros

  • ₹10,999 — lowest price in this roundup
  • Stock Android TV 11 experience
  • Decent brightness for daytime viewing

Cons

  • UI stutters during navigation
  • Thinner service network than Xiaomi/Realme
  • No Dolby Audio support

5. Hisense 32A4H 32-inch HD Smart TV

₹11,999
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound20W
OSVIDAA U
Warranty1 yr

Hisense uses its own VIDAA OS instead of Google TV. It boots fast and is responsive, but app support is weaker — Netflix and Prime work, but Disney+ Hotstar and Apple TV require workarounds. The panel is decent for the price. Hisense's Indian service network is also smaller than Xiaomi.

Pros

  • VIDAA OS is fast and responsive
  • Decent VA panel with good contrast
  • Bluetooth 5.0 — solid wireless audio

Cons

  • VIDAA has weaker app support than Google TV
  • Smaller service network in India
  • No Chromecast built-in

The one we recommend skipping

Skip

Kodak 32HDX700s — looks like a deal, isn't

₹9,999
Size/Resolution32-inch HD
Sound20W
OSWebOS-like shell
Warranty1 yr

The Kodak 32HDX700s is the cheapest 32-inch smart TV you can buy in India at ₹9,999, and the marketing leans hard on its WebOS-like interface. The reality: it's a custom Linux shell that resembles WebOS but has none of LG's app ecosystem. Netflix works, but Disney+ Hotstar, Apple TV, and most regional apps require workarounds or aren't available. Wi-Fi is single-band 2.4GHz and disconnects on weak networks. Build quality is flimsy — the stand wobbles and the bezel flexes under pressure.

The biggest issue is long-term support. Kodak TVs are manufactured by Super Plastronics, and while they offer 1-year warranty, the service network outside metro areas is thin. Software updates are inconsistent — many users report that bugs from the first month are never patched. If you want a TV that just works for 3+ years, the ₹2,000 jump to the Xiaomi TV 5A is money well spent.

The bottom line

For most buyers, the Xiaomi TV 5A at ₹12,999 is the right choice — Google TV is responsive, the panel is solid, and 2 years of warranty covers any panel burn-in or OS issues. If sound is your priority (you watch a lot of dialogue-heavy content), the Realme Smart TV at ₹11,499 wins on its 24W speakers. Avoid the Kodak — the savings aren't worth the software frustrations.

Buy a budget ₹2,500 soundbar alongside any TV in this range — the in-box speakers max out at 20–24W, and external audio makes a noticeable difference for movies and sports. If you can stretch to ₹18,000, a 43-inch FHD Xiaomi TV 5A Pro is a meaningful upgrade in size and clarity.

Frequently asked questions

Is 32-inch the only size under ₹15,000?

Mostly yes — 32-inch HD/HD-ready smart TVs dominate this range. 43-inch FHD models from Acer and Kodak occasionally drop below ₹15,000 on sale but usually sit at ₹16,000–₹18,000.

HD-ready vs Full HD under ₹15,000 — does it matter?

On a 32-inch panel viewed from 6–8 feet, HD-ready (1366x768) is fine for TV channels and OTT. If you sit closer or want sharper text on-screen, stretch to a 43-inch FHD model.

Which TV OS is best — Android, Google TV, or Fire TV?

Google TV (Android 11+) has the cleanest interface and widest app support. Fire TV works well for Amazon Prime but is heavier. WebOS (LG) and Tizen (Samsung) are smoother but have fewer apps.

Do budget TVs have good sound?

Mostly no — 20W box speakers are the ceiling. For clear dialogue and bass, budget ₹2,500 for a soundbar.

Ready to pick a TV?

Compare the top picks above and check current sale prices on Amazon and Flipkart before you buy — both platforms run festival discounts that can shave ₹1,000–₹2,000 off these prices.

Get the full comparison sheet

What about 43-inch TVs that occasionally drop under ₹15,000?

During Flipkart Big Billion Days and Amazon Great Indian Festival, 43-inch FHD smart TVs from Acer, Kodak, and VW regularly drop from ₹18,000 to ₹20,000 down to ₹14,000 to ₹15,000. If you can wait for a sale and your room has space, a 43-inch FHD panel is a meaningful upgrade in size over 32-inch HD -- text is sharper, movies feel more cinematic, and viewing angles improve for family seating. The trade-off: build quality and OS polish are noticeably weaker on the discounted 43-inch models. The Acer H Series 43-inch is the safest 43-inch pick in this range, but verify the warranty terms -- sale-period units sometimes ship with 6-month instead of 1-year coverage.

Google TV vs Android TV -- what changed in 2026?

Google TV is the newer interface built on top of Android 11+. It replaces the older Android TV launcher with a content-first home screen -- recommendations from Netflix, Prime, Disney+, and YouTube appear together, and the "For You" tab learns what you watch. Android 11 (stock, not Google TV) is what ships on the OnePlus Y1S and Acer H Series -- it works fine but the launcher is busier. For a single-user household, Google TV is noticeably better; for shared family use, either is fine.

Wall-mounting checklist under ₹15,000

Most TVs in this range are VESA 100x100 compatible -- the mount costs ₹400 to ₹800 on Amazon. The Xiaomi and Realme models weigh 3.8 to 4.2kg without the stand, so a basic fixed or tilt mount is enough. Skip articulating arms for these -- the torque makes them sag over time at this weight. If you are renting and cannot drill, a tabletop stand with rubber feet works fine; both brands include the stand in the box.

What about smart TV warranty claims?

All five picks carry 1-year comprehensive warranty (the Xiaomi 5A also covers panel burn-in for the first year). To claim warranty, you need the original invoice and the serial number from the back of the TV. Xiaomi and Realme have the fastest turnaround (3 to 5 days in metro cities, 7 to 10 days elsewhere); Acer and Hisense can take 10 to 14 days. OnePlus and Kodak are the slowest (14 to 21 days). For tier-2 and tier-3 cities, Xiaomi service network is the most reliable -- this matters if you live outside a metro.

Should I buy a TV with HDR support under ₹15,000?

Be skeptical of HDR claims at this price. HDR10 is supported on the Xiaomi 5A, Realme Smart TV, and OnePlus Y1S, but the peak brightness (typically 220 to 280 nits) is far below the 600+ nits needed for HDR to look meaningful. Dolby Vision is not available on any of these TVs in this price range. In practice, standard SDR content looks identical to "HDR" content on these panels -- the HDR logo is more of a marketing checkbox than a real visual upgrade. If you care about HDR, budget at least ₹25,000 for a TV that can do it justice.
